exact.boundary_unitarity_guard: Theta_*(r)=(r+i)/(r-i) has |Theta_*(u)|=1 for every real u but has a pole at r=i; moving a high-contour inverse Fourier integral to the real axis acquires a nonzero residue proportional to exp(x). Boundary unimodularity alone does not make the high-contour Hankel operator unitary or contractive
exact.determinant_only_reduction: A strictly decreasing cofinal omega_n->0 family with det(I+/-K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t])!=0 for every n and t already implies RH: the compatible finite forms extend to a bounded causal multiplier, and any off-line zero would generate distinct shifted zeros accumulating at itself
exact.horizontal_countermodel: F_*(z)=z^2+6*z+25 and M_*(w)=F_*(w^2) have zeros +/-1+/-2*i; |M_*(w)| is strictly increasing in Re(w) for Re(w)>1, but P_*(w^2)<0 at w=11/10+(7/5)*i
exact.horizontal_growth_theorem: Sondow-Dumitrescu: Re(xi'(s)/xi(s))>0 in every open right half-plane lying strictly to the right of all xi zeros; in particular sigma>1
exact.hyperbolic_monotonicity: For X=delta^2-tau^2 and Y=2*delta*tau: partial_Y log|xi(1/2+delta+i*tau)| at fixed X=[tau*Re(xi'/xi)-delta*Im(xi'/xi)]/[2*(delta^2+tau^2)]
exact.local_hamiltonian: For nu*omega>1, Suzuki constructs tau>0 with det(I+/-K[t])!=0 on 0<=t<tau and H(t)=diag(1/gamma(t),gamma(t)), gamma(t)=[det(I+K[t])/det(I-K[t])]^2
exact.rank_one_tn_guard: The constant Hankel kernel K(x+y)=1 on L2(0,1) is totally nonnegative and rank one, but its nonzero eigenvalue is 1, so det(I-K)=0 and det(I+K)=2
exact.spectral_target: The finite-t spectral target is pointwise-in-t strict contractivity ||K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t]||<1 for every finite t on a cofinal omega_n->0 sequence; no positive gap uniform in t is required or possible in the desired HB case
exact.suzuki_equivalence: RH iff there exist omega_n decreasing to 0 and integers nu_n with nu_n*omega_n>1 such that det(I+/-K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t])!=0 for every t>=0 and J_(omega_n,nu_n)(t;r,r)->0 as t->infinity for every r in the upper half-plane
exact.terminal_reduction: For one fixed pair the terminal limit is not a direct consequence of contractivity. Within the cofinal RH criterion, however, determinant nonvanishing first implies RH, after which Suzuki's Theorem 2.3 supplies J(t;r,r)->0
exact.xi_directional_pick: For s=sigma+i*tau, delta=sigma-1/2>0, w=2*(delta+i*tau), and xi(s)!=0: 2*|w|^2*P_Phi(w^2)/|M(w)|^2=tau*Re(xi'(s)/xi(s))-delta*Im(xi'(s)/xi(s))

polynomial_guard.conclusion: Horizontal modulus growth in Re(w)>1 does not imply the squared-variable Pick sign.

proof_boundary: This artifact proves the exact Phi-to-xi normalization, the directional and hyperbolic forms of the Pick target, and three exact countermodel guards. It records Suzuki's published unconditional local construction and exact global equivalence. It also records the internally audited determinant-only cofinal reduction. It does not prove global Fredholm nonvanishing, the Phi Pick sign, LP+, PF-infinity, Jensen hyperbolicity for zeta, RH, or Lambda<=0.

rows.claim: The Phi transform is exactly the completed xi function in the square-root coordinate.
rows.proof_boundary: The constant factor does not affect logarithmic derivatives or zero locations.

rows.claim: The global Pick sign is a directional logarithmic-derivative inequality for xi.
rows.formula: For s=sigma+i*tau, delta=sigma-1/2>0, w=2*(delta+i*tau), and xi(s)!=0: 2*|w|^2*P_Phi(w^2)/|M(w)|^2=tau*Re(xi'(s)/xi(s))-delta*Im(xi'(s)/xi(s))
rows.proof_boundary: This identity is evaluated away from zeros; strict global positivity itself excludes them.

rows.claim: The Pick target is monotonicity of |xi| along the first-quadrant hyperbolas X=constant.
rows.formula: For X=delta^2-tau^2 and Y=2*delta*tau: partial_Y log|xi(1/2+delta+i*tau)| at fixed X=[tau*Re(xi'/xi)-delta*Im(xi'/xi)]/[2*(delta^2+tau^2)]
rows.proof_boundary: It is endpoint-equivalent and is not proved here.

rows.claim: Classical horizontal xi-modulus growth controls only Re(xi'/xi).
rows.formula: Sondow-Dumitrescu: Re(xi'(s)/xi(s))>0 in every open right half-plane lying strictly to the right of all xi zeros; in particular sigma>1
rows.proof_boundary: It does not control the second directional term -delta*Im(xi'/xi).

rows.claim: A conjugate off-axis zero pair contributes with a sharp forbidden-disk sign.
rows.proof_boundary: Using actual xi zeros in this formula is diagnostic, not a noncircular proof.

rows.claim: Horizontal modulus growth strictly to the right of every zero does not imply the Pick sign.
rows.formula: F_*(z)=z^2+6*z+25 and M_*(w)=F_*(w^2) have zeros +/-1+/-2*i; |M_*(w)| is strictly increasing in Re(w) for Re(w)>1, but P_*(w^2)<0 at w=11/10+(7/5)*i
rows.proof_boundary: The witness is a finite polynomial, not xi.

rows.claim: Suzuki's shifted completed-xi family gives an arithmetic Hermite-Biehler route.
rows.proof_boundary: Membership in the Hermite-Biehler class for all omega>0 is equivalent to RH, not assumed here.

rows.claim: The inverse Fourier ratio produces a self-adjoint arithmetic Hankel operator.
rows.proof_boundary: Its kernel includes both gamma-factor and arithmetic Dirichlet-coefficient data.

rows.claim: For nu*omega>1 the operator and positive diagonal Hamiltonian exist unconditionally on a nonzero initial interval.
rows.formula: For nu*omega>1, Suzuki constructs tau>0 with det(I+/-K[t])!=0 on 0<=t<tau and H(t)=diag(1/gamma(t),gamma(t)), gamma(t)=[det(I+K[t])/det(I-K[t])]^2
rows.proof_boundary: Local existence does not prove extension to every t or the terminal condition.

rows.claim: Boundary modulus one does not justify replacing Suzuki's high-contour kernel by a unitary real-boundary multiplier.
rows.formula: Theta_*(r)=(r+i)/(r-i) has |Theta_*(u)|=1 for every real u but has a pole at r=i; moving a high-contour inverse Fourier integral to the real axis acquires a nonzero residue proportional to exp(x). Boundary unimodularity alone does not make the high-contour Hankel operator unitary or contractive
rows.proof_boundary: Contour deformation is valid only after excluding intervening poles; using innerness here would be circular.

rows.claim: Suzuki reduces RH to global Fredholm nonvanishing plus terminal canonical-kernel collapse on a cofinal omega sequence.
rows.formula: RH iff there exist omega_n decreasing to 0 and integers nu_n with nu_n*omega_n>1 such that det(I+/-K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t])!=0 for every t>=0 and J_(omega_n,nu_n)(t;r,r)->0 as t->infinity for every r in the upper half-plane
rows.proof_boundary: This is a precise equivalent target, not a proof that either global condition holds.

rows.claim: The global determinant gate is an integrated all-order Hankel-determinant hierarchy.
rows.proof_boundary: Termwise determinant signs alone do not control the alternating I-K series.

rows.claim: Total nonnegativity of the Hankel kernel does not exclude eigenvalue +1.
rows.formula: The constant Hankel kernel K(x+y)=1 on L2(0,1) is totally nonnegative and rank one, but its nonzero eigenvalue is 1, so det(I-K)=0 and det(I+K)=2
rows.proof_boundary: A strict contraction or another quantitative exclusion of +/-1 is still required.

rows.claim: Pointwise strict contractivity at every finite t would close Suzuki's Fredholm nonvanishing gate.
rows.formula: The finite-t spectral target is pointwise-in-t strict contractivity ||K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t]||<1 for every finite t on a cofinal omega_n->0 sequence; no positive gap uniform in t is required or possible in the desired HB case
rows.proof_boundary: No such all-t theorem is proved for the arithmetic kernels as omega tends to zero.

rows.claim: On a cofinal family, all-time determinant nonvanishing already implies RH and makes the terminal premise redundant.
rows.formula: A strictly decreasing cofinal omega_n->0 family with det(I+/-K_(omega_n,nu_n)[t])!=0 for every n and t already implies RH: the compatible finite forms extend to a bounded causal multiplier, and any off-line zero would generate distinct shifted zeros accumulating at itself
rows.proof_boundary: For one fixed pair the terminal limit is not a direct consequence of contractivity. Within the cofinal RH criterion, however, determinant nonvanishing first implies RH, after which Suzuki's Theorem 2.3 supplies J(t;r,r)->0

rows.claim: The abstract positive-resolvent idea is replaced by one explicit arithmetic Hankel spectral programme.
rows.formula: Prove xpsh_13 on one cofinal omega_n->0 sequence without assuming HB, zero reality, RH, or Lambda<=0
rows.proof_boundary: The Pick endpoint, Suzuki criterion, and signed-Hankel evidence remain distinct until the all-time spectral gate is proved.
